frozen_candidate_root_contribution: Root ط ي ب contributes an intrinsic POSITIVE QUALITY of a referent: being wholesome / agreeable / pure / good — pleasing to sense, sound moral judgment, or appetite, and free of contamination or foulness. Its defining anchor is the repeated explicit contrast with خبيث (khabith = foul/corrupt/impure). The residue is NOT "lawful," "beautiful in form," or "sound/fit-for-purpose," but the wholesome-agreeable-pure goodness intrinsic to the thing itself.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: Root ط ي ب contributes an intrinsic POSITIVE QUALITY of a referent: being wholesome / agreeable / pure / good — pleasing to sense, sound moral judgment, or appetite, and free of contamination or foulness. Its defining anchor is the repeated explicit contrast with خبيث (khabith = foul/corrupt/impure). The residue is NOT "lawful," "beautiful in form," or "sound/fit-for-purpose," but the wholesome-agreeable-pure goodness intrinsic to the thing itself.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across all 50 occurrences the word tags something as "good" in the sense of clean, wholesome, agreeable and unspoiled. Food/provision is "the good things" (الطيبات) that are wholesome to eat; speech can be "good/pure" (كلمة طيبة, الكلم الطيب, الطيب من القول); a wind is "favorable/pleasant" (ريح طيبة); earth for dry ablution is "clean/pure" (صعيدا طيبا); offspring, a life, dwellings, a land and a greeting are "good/wholesome"; the dying believers are received "in a good/pure state" (طيبين); and the verb طاب means "to be/become good, pleasing, or willingly content." Everywhere the root marks agreeable wholesome purity — the opposite of the foul (خبيث), which stands as its named antonym in six verses.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: FORM: ADJ (17) supplies the "quality-of-X" framing طيّب/طيّبة; N (30) is mostly the substantivized plural الطيبات "the good/wholesome things," plus abstract طوبى "bliss/good-state" (13:29) and antonymic الطيب "the good vs the foul"; V (3) supplies "to be/become good/pleasing." CONSTRUCTION: حلالا طيّبا (2:168, 5:88, 8:69, 16:114) pairs the root with حلال (lawful) — since حلال already carries legality, the root's own residue there is the ADDED wholesome quality, not "lawful." الطيب مِن القول / مِن الرزق are partitive "the good part of." PARTICIPANTS/CONTEXT vary widely: food & rizq (largest cluster), speech, persons, earth, wind, dwelling, offspring, eschatological state. Subtracting form, construction and context leaves the constant residue: wholesome-agreeable-pure goodness. The "lawful/edible" reading is a CONTEXT overlay confined to the food cluster, not the root's own contribution.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 4:4 فإن طِبْنَ لكم عن شيء منه نفسًا ("if they, of their own good pleasure, remit to you part of it"). Here the root shifts from an intrinsic quality of a thing to the volitional pleasedness/contentment of a self. It is still reconcilable: the residue is the "good/agreeable" state — the self being genuinely well-pleased and willing — the psychological instance of tayyib (cf. نفسًا "as to self"). A related edge case is صعيدا طيبا (4:43, 5:6) where the sense narrows to "ritually clean/pure earth," but purity is a core face of the same residue and is confirmed by the tayyib/khabith purity axis elsewhere. Neither breaks universal presence; both instantiate wholesome-agreeable-pure goodness rather than contradict it.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: Competing hypothesis: the root simply means "lawful/permitted (food)," given the dominant rizq/eating cluster (الطيبات, أُحلّ لكم الطيبات, يُحلّ لهم الطيبات). This is defeated by (a) حلالا طيّبا, where حلال already supplies "lawful," so طيّب must add a distinct wholesome quality; (b) non-food uses immune to legality: صعيدا طيبا (clean earth), ريح طيبة (wind), كلمة طيبة / الكلم الطيب (speech), ذرية طيبة (offspring), مساكن طيبة (dwellings), طبن نفسًا (willing self), طوبى (bliss), طبتم (39:73). "Lawful" is a contextual overlay in one cluster, not the invariant. A narrower competitor — "pleasant to the senses" — fails the moral uses (الطيب من القول; tayyib vs khabith of persons and deeds); the broader wholesome-agreeable-pure goodness subsumes sensory and moral faces alike.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Distinctive vs nearest roots. ص ل ح (صالح) = soundness/rightness/fitness (esp. functional-moral righteousness); 35:10 sets الكلم الطيّب beside العمل الصالح, showing the Quran treats them as DISTINCT — the word is tayyib (wholesome/pure), the deed is salih (right/sound). ح س ن (husn) = beauty/excellence of form or conduct; tayyib is not about beauty but wholesome purity. ح ل ل (halal) = lawful; explicitly paired-and-distinguished in حلالا طيّبا. The tayyib/khabith antonymy (3:179, 5:100, 8:37, 4:2, 24:26, plus الطيب من القول vs implied foul) is unique to this root and pins the residue to a purity/wholesomeness axis. Falsifiable: the reading would break if tayyib ever described something foul/unpleasant, or were interchangeable with "merely lawful" or "merely beautiful"; no such occurrence exists in the 50.
internal_discovery.rationale: Universal presence holds across all 50 confirmed occurrences. After subtracting FORM (adjectival quality / substantivized "good things" / verbal "become good") and CONTEXT (food, speech, persons, earth, wind, dwelling, offspring, eschatological state), a single non-empty residue remains in every case: wholesome-agreeable-pure goodness. The residue is distinctive (separable from salih, husn, halal) and falsifiable, and is positively anchored by an explicit lexical antonym خبيث appearing in six verses (3:179, 5:100, 8:37, 4:2, 24:26, 7:157). The two hardest cases — طبن نفسًا (volitional contentment) and صعيدا طيبا (ritual cleanness) — instantiate the good/pure residue rather than resist it. No occurrence forces a competing sense that the residue cannot cover; the food-law "lawful" overlay is contextual, not the root's contribution. Hence STRONG, not merely moderate: the antonymic anchoring and the breadth of non-food domains that still carry the same residue give high confidence without any percentage reasoning.

adversarial_verification.notes:
Full coverage checked (50/50 occurrences). Universal presence holds: the wholesome/agreeable/pure/good quality intrinsic to the referent is demonstrably present in every cluster — provisions/food طيبات (17:70, 5:4-5, 7:157, etc.), حلالا طيبا (2:168, 5:88, 8:69, 16:114), good speech (14:24, 22:24, 35:10), good land/dwelling/wind/life/offspring/greeting (7:58, 34:15, 10:22, 16:97, 3:38, 61:12, 9:72, 24:61), verb/state forms (4:3, 4:4, 39:73, 16:32) and طوبى (13:29). The khabith antonym anchors it explicitly in ~8 verses (2:267, 3:179, 4:2, 5:100, 7:58, 8:37, 24:26 quartet, plus khaba'ith in 7:157).

Adversarial stress-tests of the residue's stated EXCLUSIONS (not lawful / not beautiful-in-form / not fit-for-purpose) surfaced three borderline occurrences but none defeats presence: (1) البلد الطيب / بلدة طيبة (7:58, 34:15) is the strongest fit-for-purpose tension (fertility), yet 7:58's explicit خبث contrast anchors the wholesome-soil reading — productivity is a consequence, not the residue; (2) ما طاب لكم من النساء (4:3) admits a 'lawful' reading the residue excludes, but the text-grounded 'agreeable/pleasing' reading fits; (3) طبن...نفسا (4:4) extends to willing/glad consent, i.e. the soul in an agreeable state — within the residue's 'agreeable' prong. صعيدا طيبا (4:43, 5:6) falls under the residue's own 'pure/free of contamination' prong, not fit-for-purpose. All four reconcilable.

Distinctiveness confirmed from in-corpus co-occurrence: حلالا طيبا separates it from Hll (lawful); طيبات made haram in 4:160 proves طيب is legally-independent intrinsic wholesomeness; الكلم الطيب vs العمل الصالح (35:10) separates from Slh; طوبى vs حسن مآب (13:29) separates from Hsn. Mild overlap with طهر (purity) in tayammum verses, but طيب is broader (agreeable + moral + appetitive + pure). Falsifiable: the residue predicts طيب never reduces to bare lawfulness, bare formal beauty, or bare functional fitness without the wholesome-goodness quality; an occurrence carrying only an excluded sense would refute it — none found. Caveat: the residue's confident exclusions (esp. fit-for-purpose vs البلد الطيب, lawful vs 4:3) are the weakest seam, but the core wholesome quality is present in all, so unity is not broken.
